excluded_cases.reason: This case is the inverse defect shape: the buggy tree is the one that CONTAINS a null guard (`if (cache != null && key != null)`) and the fix REMOVES it because the `key != null` check silently defeats the cache, whereas the accumulated rule fires only on UNGUARDED dereferences that can NPE — a single generalized rule cannot simultaneously require the guard (for case 2's buggy tree) and forbid it (for case 4's fixed tree), so it can't fire on every covered buggy tree while staying silent on every covered fixed tree.

plan.commonality: A possibly-null value from a nullable lookup — the URL component field 'urlAddress' (left null by the no-arg constructor chain URL() / ServiceConfigURL() / URLBuilder()), the result of getServiceInfo()/getValidServiceInfo(), or an invocation-attachment lookup such as getObjectAttachmentWithoutConvert()/getAttachments().get() — is used with no null check (either method-dereferenced or passed onward as a service key/argument), so the use NPEs; guard it with a null check, early return/throw, or ternary before use.
plan.message: A possibly-null value is used without a null guard: the URL component field 'urlAddress' (left null by the no-arg constructor chain URL() / ServiceConfigURL() / URLBuilder()), the result of a nullable service-info lookup (getServiceInfo() / getValidServiceInfo(), null when no matching ServiceInfo exists), or the result of a nullable invocation-attachment lookup (getObjectAttachmentWithoutConvert() / getObjectAttachment() / getAttachments().get()). The unguarded dereference, or use of the value as a service key / method argument, throws a NullPointerException (in DubboProtocol it surfaces as a misleading NPE from a null ConcurrentHashMap key). Guard the value before using it, e.g. if (x == null) return ...; / if (x == null) throw ...; / if (x != null) { ... } / x == null ? ... : x.method().
